answer: A registrar at the jetty node hands each newcomer a seed for a Wesolowski VDF set to 72 sequential hours on one core. The proof lands on a lantern ledger, where three random peers verify it in milliseconds and co-sign an age certificate; payouts stay locked until that certificate exists. Ten thousand clones cost 720,000 core-hours, about $28,800 at $0.04, plus 50,000 tokens of bonds at 5 each. Extra GPUs add nothing, because squaring in an RSA group resists parallelism, much as a sled crossing tundra gains no speed from more dogs once the trail is one lane wide.
